newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo rebel leader wants international peace force.
newsitem.headline: Congo rebel leader wants international peace force.

text.p: Congo's former Marxist President said in an interview published on Friday that a ceasefire between his forces and those of President Pascal Lissouba would hold only if an international peace force was deployed.
"For the ceasefire to be maintained, an international force must be deployed," ex-President Denis Sassou Nguesso told the French daily newspaper Le Figaro.

Reports from the embattled capital Brazzaville said gunfire continued to rattle around the city after another day of fighting between supporters of Lissouba and his predecessor dashed hopes of a ceasefire.
Sassou Nguesso said the French army, which has more than 1,250 men in the field to protect foreign residents, could take part in the international force he wanted stationed there.
He also said a scheduled presidential election on July 27 "could not take place without international control because Lissouba's people...are no longer qualified to organise the election."
Lissouba, also interviewed by Le Figaro, said: "We are the ones who will organise the election but there can be international observers."
He said he was "neither for nor against" a peace force but feared such a deployment would delay holding the vote next month.
The interviews coincided with statements by the French military in Paris that they expected to have evacuated all French nationals and most other foreign civilians from Brazzaville within two days.

"In another 36 to 48 hours, we will have pulled out all the French and most of the other foreigners from Brazza," a military spokesman told Reuters. He did not say how many foreigners remained to be pulled out.
"Then we will be in a position where we can pull out our forces," the officer added.

He said the French troops, operating out of Brazzaville airport and making forays into the city to rescue endangered foreigners, had so far flown 3,420 foreign civilians, 1,410 of them French, out of the country.
France has said that its foreign legionnaires and marine paratroops would not intervene in the fighting and were on the spot solely to protect foreigners.
